headline: High-risk data leakage and prompt-injection pathways exist when next-ai-draw-io feeds Perplexity via files and browser-backed search; capability overlap also creates moderate conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can ingest PDFs, text, images, and diagram XML and uses MCP/browser-based AI assistance; Perplexity performs vendor-hosted browsing/search and can consume uploaded documents. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if attacker-controlled document content is passed from A into B. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF agent_a forwards untrusted document text into agent_b prompts or uploads
IF agent_b treats uploaded document content as instruction-bearing rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed system prompt that strips instructions from document text
Require a human review step before sending A outputs to B
Use a delimiter/template that labels imported text as untrusted
Disable MCP routes that can pass raw file content to B
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging from A to B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A handles API keys and broad network egress while processing PDFs, text, images, and diagrams; B uploads PDFs/images and sends browsing context to vendor-hosted services. If the same sensitive document or secret reaches both, B can transmit it off-host and A can expose it during processing. Because the pairwise data path is plausible and the blast radius includes exfiltration, high is warranted.
conditions: IF the same sensitive PDF or text file is processed by both agents
IF agent_a receives API keys or secrets in its working context
IF agent_b uploads those files or browsing context to vendor services
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared documents
Use separate workspaces for A and B
Redact API keys before any upload
Restrict B to summaries, not raw files
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/provenance controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A supports multiple instances and broad network/API use; B supports multiple instances with shared context across sessions for the same user. They do not both write the filesystem, but they can still contend over shared user-level state, uploaded artifacts, and browser sessions. The overlap is real but not the high-severity same-directory write conflict, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same user session or shared workspace
IF agent_a and agent_b update the same uploaded artifact or browser state
mitigations: Assign separate sessions per agent
Avoid concurrent edits to the same artifact
Serialize handoffs through one operator
Clear browser state between runs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces AI-assisted visualizations and document transformations; B is a search-RAG answer engine with citations. If B consumes A's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into B's cited answers or actions. The profiles do not prove automatic trust, but the documented workflow makes the pathway plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as source material without verification
IF A-generated diagram text or summaries are reused in B answers
mitigations: Require source verification before B cites A output
Have B quote only primary sources
Mark A output as draft/untrusted
Add a checklist for factual cross-checking
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware citation gating

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source and handles API keys plus documents; B is closed-source, vendor-hosted, and uploads PDFs/images while retaining shared context across sessions for the same user. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch for the same data class, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated data type like PHI or EU PII, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into documents processed by both agents
IF the operator expects B's vendor-hosted retention to match A's local handling
mitigations: Do not send regulated data to B
Review B retention settings before use
Separate datasets by jurisdiction
Document which agent stores what data
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class
